paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend: God cares about the heart more than the hand-washing. The Pharisees and scribes had a long list of traditions, and they kept it spotless. Jesus quotes Isaiah about them: "These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me." (Mark 7:6) A tradition can look so holy and still leave the heart untouched, and that is what He is warning about.

Jesus also shows what happens when people hold tighter to their own rules than to God's word. He says, "You have disregarded the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men." (Mark 7:8) Corban is His example, and it shows how a rule that sounds devoted to God can end up cutting a person off from honoring their father and mother (Mark 7:10-12). So the question for us is not just "Am I following the rules?" It's "Am I following GOD?"

Then Jesus turns to the crowd and gets to the root. Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him, because it goes into the stomach and not the heart, and "All these evils come from within, and these are what defile a man." (Mark 7:19, 23) That is good news, friend, because Jesus is not asking you to scrub harder on the outside. He is pointing you to the heart, and that is where God wants to work in you. Bring the heart to Him first, and let the rest follow.
